analysis:
The only change in this PR is a documentation-only addition at docs/architecture/inference.md head lines 49-64. It describes a Gated DeltaNet four-row recurrence kernel for qwen3_5, qwen3_5_moe and prism_hadamard_qwen35 prompt windows. Each kernel instantiation is probed once per process, and the first of the `packed` and `rows` kernels that reproduces `gated_delta_step` bit for bit on the GPU is kept, otherwise the stock kernel. Decode, MTP verification, masked updates and short windows stay on the stock kernel. A `DARKBLOOM_TTFT_GDN_BLOCKED` override is documented. The base-side units (4, 5) show only unchanged surrounding MiMo and Qwen4 text and add nothing new.

No trust boundary, authorization, attestation, encryption or data-exposure control changes. The prose depends on code outside the supplied evidence: GatedDelta.swift, whose bit-exact probe and fallback behavior cannot be verified here, and the env var parsing. The text states that mixing kernels cannot change the recurrent state used by checkpoint capture. That is a correctness claim relevant to the T-041 prefix-cache and complete-checkpoint behavior, but it is not demonstrated here.

T-041 is the closest relevant threat. Per-process kernel selection and any timing difference between kernels do not alter the accepted TTFT oracle in kind, because cache scope, HMAC naming and TTL are untouched. The doc says nothing about SSD cache gating or the DBK3 format. The env override is operator-local and, per the existing deadline guard docs, performance-affecting DARKBLOOM_* keys already disqualify deadline profiles. This PR does not assert otherwise.

The one remaining question for integration is whether the actual kernel code, outside this doc-only patch, honors the bit-exact fallback. That is outside this PR's supplied evidence, so I record it here and raise no finding.
